summary: Our team developed Cloudynow: a web tool that translates NASA POWER climate data (10+ years, ~50 km) into crop rotation guidance for smallholder farmers in El Salvador's Dry Corridor. In a 3-step no-login flow —location, farm profile, results— it compares 3 rotations (current, +cover crop, drought-tolerant swap) with transparent rule-based scores across 5 criteria (Water, Soil, Erosion, Income, Risk) citing NASA evidence. It addresses the Cambio de campo challenge by bridging satellite data to actionable agronomic decisions. It matters because farmers rely on generational experience while climate patterns shift; the tool supports, does not replace their judgment, democratizing climate science for local food security.
details:
Cloudynow is a 3-step no-login web app: 1) Pick location on El Salvador map (or search town) → 2) Select current crops (1–4) and priority (water/income/soil) → 3) Compare 3 rotations (current, +cover crop, drought-tolerant swap) with transparent scores across 5 criteria (Water, Soil, Erosion, Income, Risk) citing NASA POWER evidence. Serverless backend computes 10-year climate indicators (rainfall, dry spell, heat, soil moisture) and applies priority-weighted rule-based scoring.

Benefits:

- Democratizes satellite climate data for agronomic decisions

- Transparent: every score shows evidence, benefits, risks, gaps

- No login, free, works offline with fallback data

- "Similar options" flag (< 0.05 diff) and low-confidence warning (CV > 0.2)

Intended impact:

Smallholders in the Dry Corridor make planting decisions backed by data, not just experience. Reduces crop-loss risk, optimizes water use, improves soil health. Scalable to any region with NASA POWER coverage.

Tools/languages:

- Frontend: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, MapLibre GL, Recharts, React Router, i18next

- Backend: Node.js 20+ ES modules, Vercel serverless, no DB, no runtime deps

- Data: NASA POWER Daily API (T2M, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M, GWETROOT), static JSON (zones, crops, fallback)

- Place search: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap)

- Deploy: Vercel (2 projects), GitHub

- Testing: Jest (58 backend tests), ESLint

Creativity:

- Translates complex climate science into 3 comparable cards in seconds

- "Similar" rule (< 0.05) and auto confidence note (CV > 0.2) — prevents false precision

- Bare-field window computed from real data, not assumed

- Mobile-first, no-scroll, accessible design

Factors considered:

- NASA POWER resolution (~50 km) → explicit UI limitation

- Crop traits in crops.json are drafts (needsValidation: true) → require MAG/CENTA/FAO validation

- No local soil, prices, pests → listed as gaps in every result

- Canícula (mid-summer drought) → dry spell calculated May–Oct, not full year

- Farmer expertise → tool supports, does not replace (disclaimer in every response)
